fig20_1: Four semilog and heatmap panels in a two-by-two grid dissecting the two-parameter error surface for domain truncation of hyperbolic-secant of y. Panel (a) fixes truncation length L at six and varies resolution N: the error falls then flattens onto a horizontal floor at e to the power minus L, about two point five times ten to the power minus three, marked by a navy dashed line. Panel (b) fixes N at thirty-two and varies L, tracing a V-shaped curve with a broad minimum near L equal to six. Panel (c) grows N and L together, giving a slow subgeometric descent down to three times ten to the power minus five at N, L equal to ninety-six, fourteen. Panel (d) is a heatmap of log base ten of the error over the N-L plane, dark good and yellow bad, with the three sweeps overlaid as polylines, showing they are horizontal, vertical, and diagonal cuts through one surface.
fig20_2: Two panels comparing Fourier and Chebyshev truncation of hyperbolic-secant of y on the interval minus ten to ten. The left panel shows the two collocation grids as point distributions: the Fourier grid is uniformly dense across the interior, while the Chebyshev grid clusters points near the far edges where the solution is already below ten to the power minus four. The right panel is a semilog plot of interior max-norm error versus N: the Fourier curve sits two to three orders of magnitude lower than Chebyshev until they cross near N equal to one hundred, where Chebyshev's geometric tail finally overtakes.
fig20_3: Four panels analysing the sinc expansion of hyperbolic-secant of y. Panel (a) is a semilog plot of error versus grid spacing h at fixed N equal forty-eight, forming a V whose left branch is bandwidth error and right branch is grid-span error; the empirical minimum, navy dotted, coincides with the theoretical square root of pi squared over two N, teal dashed. Panel (b) decomposes the V into its two competing analytic curves, a navy dashed bandwidth term and a coral dashed grid-span term, whose teal sum recovers the grey empirical V and whose crossing marks the optimum. Panel (c) plots max-norm error versus square root of N at optimal h, a straight descending line confirming the subgeometric rate exponential of minus pi times square root of N over two. Panel (d) is a grid cartoon at N equal eight and thirty-two showing that quadrupling N doubles the span and halves the spacing.
fig20_4: Six panels in a three-by-two grid on Hermite-function expansion of Gaussian targets e to the power minus A y squared. Panel (a) overlays four target Gaussians for A of zero point one, zero point five, two, and eight against the dashed grey unscaled basis envelope, with A equal one half tracking it exactly. Panel (b) plots coefficient magnitude versus index at A equal eight: the unscaled coral curve decays slowly and algebraically while the matched navy case has only the first coefficient nonzero. Panel (c) shows unscaled convergence where only A equal one half is exact and the rest converge slowly. Panel (d) shows matched scaling alpha equal square root of two A collapsing all four curves to machine precision at every N. Panel (e) scans alpha at fixed N equal sixteen for three A values, each curve dipping sharply at alpha equal square root of two A marked by dotted verticals. Panel (f) shows the oscillator ground state reaching machine precision already at N equal zero.
fig20_5: Two semilog convergence panels comparing the Laguerre basis against rational Chebyshev T-L-n on the half-line. The left panel uses the pure exponential e to the power minus y: both bases descend geometrically to machine precision, with Laguerre slightly faster. The right panel uses the algebraic one over one plus y: the Laguerre curve flattens onto a plateau near ten to the power minus three because its exponential envelope cannot follow the one-over-y tail, while T-L-n keeps descending to machine precision by N equal thirty-two.
fig20_6: Two panels demonstrating where Hermite fails. The left panel plots the smooth bell-shaped target one over one plus y squared. The right panel is a log-log error-versus-N comparison of three bases: Hermite and sinc both decay only algebraically, roughly as one over square root of N, while the rational Chebyshev T-B-n curve plunges straight to machine precision by N equal eight because the function lies exactly in the span of T-B-zero and T-B-two when the map parameter equals one.
fig20_7: Two panels comparing two solution strategies for Boyd's Laguerre eigenvalue problem. The left panel plots the count of accurate eigenvalues, within five percent of an integer, versus N: the naive Strategy A in coral reaches thirty-three by N equal one hundred twenty, while the recast Strategy B in teal reaches forty-nine. The right panel plots the computed spectrum in the complex plane at N equal forty: Strategy A's coral circles spread off the real axis into complex-conjugate pairs with imaginary parts around zero point zero one, signalling contamination, whereas Strategy B's teal squares lie cleanly on the real axis at integer eigenvalues lambda-n equal n.
fig20_8: Two panels on the Yoshida jet velocity profile. The left panel plots the antisymmetric profile v of y, with a high-mode reference curve and low-order truncations overlaid; even the N equal three truncation matches the reference to three decimals across the interior. The right panel is a semilog convergence plot showing the odd S-B basis, which matches the minus-one-over-y algebraic tail by construction, descending rapidly to about ten to the power minus five by N equal ten.
fig20_9: Four panels in a two-by-two grid illustrating the rational Chebyshev T-L-n map on the half-line. Panel (a) plots the algebraic map y equal ell times one plus x over one minus x for four map parameters, each rising steeply toward the singularity at x equal one that sends the unit interval to the half-line, with larger ell delaying the rise. Panel (b) shows the resulting collocation grids at N equal twenty-four as horizontal tick rows over a grey decaying target: small ell packs nodes near the origin, large ell scatters them far out. Panel (c) plots the first five basis functions over y from zero to twenty, each asymptoting to plus or minus one at infinity. Panel (d) plots coefficient magnitude versus index for the expansion of hyperbolic-secant at three ell values, where too-small ell flattens early, too-large ell has a gentle slope, and ell about two descends fastest.
fig20_10: Four panels in a two-by-two grid on diagnosing the map parameter ell from coefficient decay. Panel (a) shows rolling-max coefficient envelopes at N equal sixty-four for three regimes: ell equal zero point five flattens onto an early plateau, ell equal sixteen has a gentler small-index slope, and ell equal two descends cleanly to machine precision. Panel (b) overlays envelopes for a full six-ell sweep for direct comparison. Panel (c) plots the scalar tail-sum diagnostic versus ell for three values of N, each forming a valley whose broad minimum marks the good range and widens with N. Panel (d) extracts the valley centre and width versus N on log-log axes, the centre drifting mildly upward and the width growing, so larger problems tolerate coarser tuning.
fig20_11: Two panels on a single global expansion of r times K-one of r. The left panel overlays the navy reference function and its coral dashed N equal sixteen T-B-n approximation in the composed coordinate, agreeing within the line thickness across a peak that decays to zero. The right panel is a semilog plot of max-norm error versus N for map parameter four, descending steadily to ten to the power minus ten at N equal sixty-four, achieved with one global expansion and no piecewise switching.
fig20_12: Two panels on asymptotic augmentation for square root of one plus y times J-zero of y. The left panel shows the target alongside its amplitude-phase decomposition at N equal fifteen: the amplitude magnitude settles to a constant near zero point eight nine and the phase magnitude tends to zero, confirming the expected WKB structure. The right panel is a semilog plot of max-norm error over zero to fifty versus N: the naive basis stays pinned near one, unable to resolve the oscillation, while the augmented basis plunges to ten to the power minus thirteen by N equal twenty.
fig20_13: Four panels in a two-by-two grid on the Weideman-Cloot sinh map. Panel (a) plots y equal hyperbolic-sine of ell times t for four ell values, with the annotated reach hyperbolic-sine of ell pi growing exponentially, from about two at ell equal zero point five to near two hundred seventy at ell equal two. Panel (b) shows the resulting grids at N equal sixty-four as tick rows over a hyperbolic-secant target, the uniform t-grid mapping to a y-grid compressed near the origin and stretched into the tails. Panel (c) shows the same target in y-space, navy, and in rescaled t-space, coral dashed, where it becomes a smooth periodic-friendly profile that Fourier handles efficiently. Panel (d) plots Fourier coefficient magnitude versus index for four ell values, the optimal ell being the one whose coefficients descend furthest before flattening.
